record.paper_title: A collection of open problems in celebration of Imre Leader’s 60th birthday
record.context_brief: Weak upper bound for chromatic-intersecting families
record.original_question: Does there exist an absolute constant c > 0 such that for every t ≥ 3, any family F of labeled graphs on vertex set [n] whose pairwise intersections all have chromatic number at least t satisfies |F| ≤ 2^{(n choose 2) - c t^2}?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.4. There exists an absolute constant c > 0 such that the following holds. Let t ≥ 3. If F ⊂ P(([n] choose 2)) is a family of labelled graphs on the vertex-set [n] such that for all G, H ∈ F, G ∩ H has chromatic number at least t, then |F| ≤ 2^((n choose 2)−ct2).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 1$ and $t\ge 3$ be integers. Identify a labeled graph on the vertex set $[n]=\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ with its edge set, a subset of $\binom{[n]}{2}$, and let $\mathcal{P}\bigl(\binom{[n]}{2}\bigr)$ denote the set of all such labeled graphs. For two graphs $G,H$ on $[n]$, write $G\cap H$ for the graph on $[n]$ whose edge set is the intersection of the edge sets of $G$ and $H$, and let $\chi(\,\cdot\,)$ denote the chromatic number.

Call a family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq \mathcal{P}\bigl(\binom{[n]}{2}\bigr)$ \emph{$t$-chromatic-intersecting} if for every $G,H\in\mathcal{F}$ one has $\chi(G\cap H)\ge t$.

Decide whether the following statement is true: there exists an absolute constant $c>0$ such that for every integer $t\ge 3$, every integer $n\ge 1$, and every $t$-chromatic-intersecting family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq \mathcal{P}\bigl(\binom{[n]}{2}\bigr)$,
$$|\mathcal{F}|\;\le\;2^{\binom{n}{2}-c\,t^2}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture appears to be open. A closely related conjecture of Ellis–Filmus–Friedgut for $K_t$-intersecting families (which would imply the chromatic version up to constants) is known for $t=3$ (Ellis–Filmus–Friedgut) and $t=4$ (Berger–Zhao), but remains open for $t\ge 5$. A recent paper on $H$-intersecting graph families only establishes the much weaker bound $2^{\binom{n}{2}-(\chi(H)-1)}$, linear in $t$, not quadratic.

status_evidence.title: On H-Intersecting Graph Families and Counting of Homomorphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture 2.1 (Ellis, Filmus, Friedgut): |G| ≤ 2^{(n choose 2) - t(t-1)/2}. t=3 proven; t=4 recently proven (Berger and Zhao); t ≥ 5 open. Our bound: |G| ≤ 2^{(n choose 2) - (χ(H)-1)}, linear in t.
status_evidence.claim: The quadratic bound for chromatic/clique intersecting families remains open for t ≥ 5, and best general bound for chromatic intersection is only linear in t.
